hints.content:
We are trying to find a **unit rate**, specifically the price per $1$ night.

$\dfrac{\blueE{\text{total price}}}{\maroonD{\text{nights}}} = \purpleD{\text{price per night}}$

We can compare from the largest to the smallest place value.

###Finding the unit rates

We divide based on the unit rate we want, not the order of the columns in the original table.

Hotel| $\blueE{\text{Price}} $ || $\maroonD{\text{Nights}}$||$\purpleE{\text{Price per night}}$ 
- | :-: | :-:| :-:|:-:|:-:
$A$ |$192$|$\div$ | $3$|$=$|$64$
$B$|$300$ |$\div$ |$5$ | $=$|$60$
$C$ |$455$ |$\div$ | $7$|$=$| $65 $

###Comparing the unit rates

Hotel | Tens | Ones
- | :-: | :-:| :-:|:-:|:-:
$A$ | $6$ | $4$
$B$| $6$ | $\redE{0}$
$C$ | $6$ | $5$

The hotels all cost $6$ tens of dollars per night, but hotel B costs the least ones of dollars per night.

###Conclusion

Hotel $B$ costs the least per night.

question.content:
The price per night for a hotel room is different at three different hotels. 

Hotel | Nights | Price (in dollars)
- | :-: | :-:
$A$ | $3$ | $192$
$B$ | $5$ | $300$
$C$ | $7$ | $455$

**Which hotel costs the least per night?**

[[☃ radio 1]]
